numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When negating the point at infinity, the result was a non-canonical infinity point `(0, -1, 0)` so `(neg_O.x, neg_O.y, neg_O.z) != (O.x, O.y, O.z)`.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Negating the point at infinity should return the canonical infinity point `(0, 1, 0)`, so the coordinates match.
trigger_conditions: The point being negated has `z == 0` (i.e., it is the point at infinity).

input_output_examples.input: from sympy.ntheory.elliptic_curve import EllipticCurve, EllipticCurvePoint; E = EllipticCurve(0, 0); O = EllipticCurvePoint.point_at_infinity(E); neg_O = -O; (neg_O.x, neg_O.y, neg_O.z)
input_output_examples.source: issue#28546 repro + PR#28567 description (canonical vs non-canonical infinity points)

oracle_clues: Regression assertion checks coordinate tuple equality: `assert (neg_O.x, neg_O.y, neg_O.z) == (O.x, O.y, O.z)`.
PR description states canonical infinity is `(0, 1, 0)` and the buggy non-canonical result was `(0, -1, 0)`.
Code fix added: `if self.z == 0: return self.point_at_infinity(self._curve)`.

category_specific_evidence: Mathematical property violated: negation should preserve the point at infinity representation, i.e. for the infinity point O, we must have -O == O (component-wise comparison of the homogeneous coordinates).

Concrete failing values (from reproducer): E = EllipticCurve(0, 0), O = EllipticCurvePoint.point_at_infinity(E), neg_O = -O, and the assertion (neg_O.x, neg_O.y, neg_O.z) == (O.x, O.y, O.z) raised an AssertionError.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction depends on the internal representation of the point at infinity; the fix changes canonical infinity from (0, -1, 0) to (0, 1, 0).
If the test only checks equality via a method/operator rather than comparing raw (x,y,z) tuples, the observed mismatch may differ from the provided assertion-based reproducer.
